title: What a proof of the arm inequality must contain
claim: For a gadget of a non-windable knot and a linked difference pattern d, the configurations compatible with d inject into those compatible with d xor arm(d), so the arm inequality holds whenever d -> d xor arm(d) is injective, as on trees. For any function on three bits, the arm inequality for the axes u and u + e_i together is equivalent to |minor| <= agree + cross in the table of terminal i against terminals j, k, and to 2F(u)F(u-bar) <= G(A)G(Abar) + the j and k split products, with G (terminal i free) positive on every pattern of a native gadget by co-independence. Explicit gadgets of two or three knots satisfy the arm inequality but fail the bound per partner solution, per image pattern, for one-sided path-flip matchings, and without the agreeing terms, so any proof for gadgets with cycles must be global.
failure_conditions: A linked difference pattern whose compatible configurations do not inject as stated.
A tree gadget on which d -> d xor arm(d) is not injective.
The symmetric forms are not equivalent to the arm inequality, or G vanishes on some pattern.
A stored witness does not fail its strengthening, or violates the arm inequality.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite gadgets of the open knots; structural statements and explicit witnesses; the arm inequality for gadgets with cycles stays open. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library) verifies Lemma 1 on 15,582 linked patterns of 300 gadgets (184 trees), the identities of Proposition 2 on 20,000 random functions and positivity of G on 2,000 gadgets, and the four witnesses exactly; three controls. No human or external review
